question.text: A Rs. 10 cr bond has PD = 2%, LGD = 40%. What is the Expected Loss?

explanation.text: The Logic: In standard credit-risk practice, Expected Loss is the product of the three credit-risk components: Probability of Default (PD), Loss Given Default (LGD) and Exposure at Default (EAD). For this bond: EL = 0.02 × 0.40 × Rs. 10 cr = Rs. 8 lakh. The Trap: Rs. 2 lakh uses only PD × EAD and ignores recovery (LGD); Rs. 40 lakh uses LGD × EAD without conditioning on default probability; Rs. 2 cr is just LGD × EAD inflated and has no credit-loss interpretation. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook lists the three components of credit risk (around pp. 296 and 346) but the checked text does not state the Expected Loss = PD × LGD × EAD formula in that explicit form. The calculation above is based on the standard credit-risk industry formula rather than a direct workbook quote.
